strategy.summary: Identify 1-hour intermediate term structure to establish the draw on liquidity, wait for price to reach a 1-hour PD array during a New York killzone, and enter using a 1-minute or 5-minute pattern.

timeframes.notes: Uses 1-hour intermediate term highs/lows for direction and PD arrays. Entry is strictly executed on either the 1-minute or 5-minute timeframe.

glossary.8:30/9:30 rule: If 8:30 AM already taps a PD array and displaces away, 9:30 AM will likely not sweep whatever 8:30 created.
glossary.1-minute entry pattern: Requires two consecutive fair value gaps in the direction of the trade before entering on the second one.
glossary.5-minute entry pattern: Requires only one fair value gap in the direction of the trade to enter.

custom_signals.name: two_fvg_entry_1m
custom_signals.plain_definition: On the 1-minute chart, price must print two consecutive FVGs in the direction of the trade. The entry is on the second FVG.

custom_signals.name: one_fvg_entry_5m
custom_signals.plain_definition: On the 5-minute chart, price must print one FVG in the direction of the trade to enter.

custom_signals.name: 830_expansion_rule
custom_signals.plain_definition: If price displaces from a PD array at 8:30, 9:30 will not sweep the 8:30 extreme.

sequence: Identify intermediate term highs and lows on the 1-hour timeframe to determine the structural draw on liquidity.
Wait for price to retrace into a 1-hour PD array (e.g., a fair value gap) in a premium or discount relative to the range.
Wait for time to align with a Killzone (8:30 AM, 9:30 AM equities open, or PM session).
Apply the 8:30/9:30 rule: if 8:30 already taps the PD array and displaces, 9:30 will not sweep what 8:30 created.
Drop down to a lower timeframe (1-minute or 5-minute) when inside the 1-hour PD array during the Killzone.
For the 1-minute timeframe, wait for two consecutive fair value gaps to form in the trade direction and enter on the second one.
For the 5-minute timeframe, wait for one fair value gap to form in the trade direction and enter on it.

invalidation.text: If the 1-hour intermediate term structure high/low is violated, the setup and bias are invalidated.

filters.text: Do not trade London session for US indices like ES, NQ, or YM; wait for New York sessions.
Choose either the 1-minute or 5-minute entry model and stick to it; do not use both simultaneously.

entry_rule.text: Enter on the second FVG on the 1-minute chart, or the first FVG on the 5-minute chart, after tapping the 1H PD array.
entry_rule.quote: once you have that second fair value Gap lower that is exactly when you want to get involved

target_rule.text: Target the 1-hour intermediate term low (for shorts) or high (for longs).
target_rule.quote: the obvious draw liquidity is what it's this low right it's that intermediate term low that is our first Target

stop_rule.text: Place stop loss beyond the short-term high/low that formed during the entry.
stop_rule.quote: what do you cover you can cover that high why that high that is a shortterm high that should hold

management.breakeven: Move to breakeven based on structural displacements and short-term highs holding.

presenter_claims.claim: You can get a 1 to 2 Risk:Reward ratio in less than 10 minutes using the 1-minute entry pattern.

strategy.notes: The strategy acts as a standalone system eliminating the need for a daily bias, relying strictly on 1H structure to define the immediate draw on liquidity.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price stings into the 1H FVG at 9:23 AM.
Price pushes into the premium array again at the 9:30 AM open and displaces lower.
A second 1-minute FVG forms lower; price retraces into it for the entry.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price pushes higher at 9:30 AM to sweep a swing high into a daily PD array.
Immediate rejection lower, showing that bullish FVGs are not being respected.
The first 5-minute FVG forms but does not get tapped by a retracement.
A new 5-minute FVG forms lower; price retraces into it, triggering the entry.

examples.presenter_commentary: Demonstrates the 5-minute variant where only one FVG is needed for entry. He emphasizes that if the first FVG isn't tapped, wait to enter on the next valid one that forms.
